title: A Salt section's or collection's editor fields, defined once for both platforms
description:
One file per section in contract/fields/<section id>.json, plus contract/fields/_section-settings.json for the wrapper settings every section carries; and one file per collection source in contract/collections/<source id>.json (the fields of a service, a case study, a post and the rest, as an editor stores them), plus contract/collections/_<shape>.json for a shape more than one record carries (person, address, topic). A file describes a section ('section'), a collection ('collection') or a shape ('shape'), exactly one. Salt for Next.js generates Payload fields from these files and Salt for WordPress generates ACF fields from them, a section's as a block or a layout and a collection's as the fields of its documents (SC-003: names, types, choices, limits and descriptions must match). Neither platform is the reference (SC-001): where they disagreed, each file records the canonical definition and, under platforms.<platform>, what that platform called it before and what it owes.

FIELD TYPES are limited to what both Payload and ACF Pro can express, and the list is closed: a type outside it is refused. text (Payload text; ACF text, with salt.format url or email for the sanitiser when it has a format, as ACF's url field refuses the mailto and tel addresses the url format allows; email is a format of text, as url is). textarea. rich-text (Payload Lexical; ACF wysiwyg), with an allowed list of element kinds. image (Payload upload; ACF image, or gallery when many). link (a fixed shape: label, type internal|external, document, url, newTab; Payload group; ACF group or link; its type is a radio). select (Payload select; ACF select. With control radio, a radio on both: the contract says which selects are radios, the stored value is the same, and a radio's layout stays native). boolean (Payload checkbox; ACF true_false). number. list (Payload array; ACF repeater). group (both group). relationship (Payload relationship; ACF relationship or post_object) to a source id from contract/sections.json. collection-query (the shared 'pick items from a source' control, below). topics (the record's own collection's topics, its category terms: Payload relationship to the source's taxonomy collection; ACF taxonomy). date-time (a moment, stored as an ISO 8601 date and time in UTC and drawn in the site's time zone: Payload date with the day-and-time picker; ACF date_time_picker). time (a time of day, stored as HH:MM on the 24-hour clock: ACF time_picker returning H:i; Payload has no picker that stores a time alone, so a text field the site draws with its own time picker). sections (a list of sections from contract/sections.json, each stored as on a page: Payload blocks; ACF flexible_content), used by a collection only.

NAMES are canonical ids, camelCase ASCII, unique among siblings, and stable: renaming one is a MAJOR (RELEASE-POLICY.md section 2). Option values are lower-case kebab ids. Empty-string option values are not allowed; a 'nothing chosen' choice gets a word (auto, focal-point, default).

CONDITIONS show a field only when a SIBLING field (same object: section, row or group) equals a value, is one of several values, or is filled (filled: true) or empty (filled: false) (SC-006). equals and in name only a select or a boolean; filled may name a sibling of any type but group, list, collection-query and link (an ACF group on WordPress), which ACF conditional logic cannot target; the gate enforces this, as a schema cannot see a sibling's type. An array of clauses means all must hold. No other expression form exists: no paths, no parent or root data. Where a platform used one, the field carries no condition, its description says when it applies, and the platform's note records the dropped condition.

NATIVE STORAGE. On Salt for WordPress a collection field stored in WordPress's own place for it (the post title, the body, the excerpt, the featured image, the categories, the date, or a term's own description) says so in platforms.wordpress.native; the ACF emitter generates no ACF field for it and records where it lives.

SHARED SETTINGS. Every section file names the shared wrapper settings in 'shared'; they live in contract/fields/_section-settings.json and are stored in a group named 'settings' on each section. A section may change a shared field's default ('defaults') or leave a shared field out ('omit'). The settings file itself has section id 'section-settings' and must not carry 'shared' (the if/then at the end of this schema); no section in contract/sections.json may take that id. A collection file may name the person shape the same way ('shared': { 'id': 'person' }); its fields are carried flat, at the top of the record, before the collection's own.

COLLECTION-QUERY stores one object of this fixed shape. mode: automatic (the collection's usual order) | by-category | manual; default automatic. categories: terms from the source's own category taxonomy, many, shown when mode is by-category, and only offered for a source that has categories. items: hand-picked items of the source, many, in the order picked, shown when mode is manual. order: default (the collection's usual order) | newest | title (A to Z), shown unless mode is manual. count: whole number from 0 to 'max' (default 24), 0 meaning the section's default for that source, shown unless mode is manual. 'source' fixes the source; 'sourceField' names a sibling select whose value picks it.

THE LIMITS RULE (ID-3968, the founder's ruling of 18/11/2026) governs every limit a field carries (maxLength, maxLines, min, max). A limit never stops a draft from saving and never cuts what an editor wrote: the editor sees the count as they type, the limit is checked when content is published, and a write that cannot show an editor the message is either refused with a message to whoever sent it or stored and flagged until fixed. A length the design only prefers is a target, shown to the editor and never refused. Lengths count Unicode code points, with a CRLF line break counting as one. The numbers are each field's own; the rule says how a platform holds them, so a platform that refuses a draft over a limit, or cuts the text, does not conform. A field that keeps a limit names it with maxLength, min or max; one whose number is only preferred names it with target in its place (below).

GATE JOBS JSON Schema cannot do here, for a later script: sibling names unique; a condition's field names an existing sibling; a select default is one of its options; rowLabel names a child field; every source id exists in contract/sections.json; every variant in sections.json appears as a select with the same values; a filled clause names no group, list, collection-query or link.

section.description: The section id from contract/sections.json, or 'section-settings' for the shared wrapper settings file. A file names a section, a collection or a shape, exactly one.

collection.description: The collection source id (contract/sections.json sources, the schema's $defs.source) whose records these fields describe. The file is contract/collections/<source id>.json.

shape.description: A shape more than one record carries: person (a team member, whom a post credits as its author), address (a location's and the company's), topic (a collection's category term). The file is contract/collections/_<shape>.json.

label.description: A collection's name for one record, singular: the title of its field group on WordPress.

shared.description: The shared fields this file carries: a section's shared settings (section-settings), stored in a group named 'settings'; or, on a collection, the person shape (person), carried flat at the top of the record.

defaults.description: Shared field name to this section's default for it.

omit.description: Shared fields this section does not carry.

dropped.description: On a collection: what a platform stores today that the contract drops, each with the platform's former name and why. A platform owes removing it, or migrating its content where the note says where.

name.description: A canonical field name: camelCase ASCII. Stable; renaming is a MAJOR.

value.description: A stored option value: a lower-case kebab id, digits allowed.

source.description: A source id from contract/sections.json that holds items (not 'inline').

field.description: A sibling field's name. Paths are not names, so a parent's or another row's field cannot be reached.

filled.description: true: the sibling has a value (a text, textarea or rich text with something visible left after removing whitespace and the zero-width characters U+200B to U+200D, U+2060 and U+FEFF, so text of nothing else is empty for conditions and for rendering (SC-009); a chosen image, option or relationship; a ticked boolean or any number; a group, list, collection-query or link cannot be tested, which the gate enforces). false: it has none. A clause tests filled or compares a value, never both. Salt for WordPress: ACF conditional logic's 'has any value' cannot express the text rule, so an editor who types only spaces still sees the dependent field, while the render treats the text as empty.

condition.description: Show this field only when a sibling equals a value, is one of several values, or is filled or empty. An array means every clause must hold.

formerly.description: The field name or path this platform used before the contract; several when fields fold into one.

values.description: Former stored value to the contract's: flat, or keyed by a part of a composite field (a collection-query's mode, for example).

formerlyEnum.description: On Salt for Next.js only, and only on a select or a collection-query: the Postgres enum type a select's column had before the contract's (emit/payload.mjs gives the new name as the field's enumName); several when types fold into one. A select records the name or names; a collection-query records them keyed by its part (mode, order). A migration renames the type, or moves the column to the contract's type where several fold into one.

owes.description: What this platform must add or change to conform.

native.description: Salt for WordPress only, on a collection's field: the field is stored in WordPress's own place for it, not in an ACF field (the ruling of 18/11/2026 on native storage). title: the post title. body: the post content. excerpt: the post excerpt. featured-image: the featured image. categories: the post type's category taxonomy, in WordPress's own box. date: the post date. description: a term's own description. The ACF emitter generates no field for it and records it under the group's salt.native.

description.description: Editor help text, the same on both platforms.

maxLength.description: The most characters the text may hold. A limit, held by the limits rule (above): a draft outside it still saves, nothing an editor wrote is cut, and it is checked when the content is published. The editor sees the count as they type. Counted in Unicode code points, a CRLF line break as one. ACF records it under salt.maxLength, never as ACF's maxlength, which cuts typing. The Payload emitter gives it as Payload's maxLength, which counts UTF-16 units (an emoji two, a CRLF two) and skips a draft only on a collection with versions.drafts on, so Salt for Next.js owes counting it in code points with a CRLF as one and never refusing a draft; how it meets that is its own.

target.description: A number the design only prefers, in place of a limit or beside one (ID-3969, the founder's ruling of 18/11/2026): for a text, a number of characters, counted in code points with a CRLF as one; for a list, a gallery or a relationship, a number of items. It is shown to the editor beside the count and never refused, on a draft save or on publish. The title of a collection whose records have a page of their own (a service, a case study, a post) carries a target of 60, measured with the site name joined as the page's <title> draws it: the page's whole <title> should be at most 60 characters, so a longer site name leaves less room for the title. An FAQ's question, a testimonial's and a team member's name and a location's title carry a target of 60 too; they have no page of their own, so whether theirs measures the field alone or they have no target is pending the founder (rc.8). ACF records a target under the field's salt.target, or, for a field WordPress stores in its own place (every collection title, name and question), under its group's salt.targets by the field's name; Payload under custom.salt.target. Neither is a setting that refuses anything. Turning a limit into a target is renaming maxLength or max to target; changing a target is a PATCH (RELEASE-POLICY.md section 2).

format.description: email: an email address (one @, a domain with a dot, no spaces), checked on save; on WordPress an ACF text field carrying salt.format 'email' and on Payload a text field carrying custom.salt.format 'email', as the url format is. url: an absolute address (http, https, mailto or tel); on WordPress an ACF text field carrying salt.format 'url', which the sanitiser reads. anchor: slugified on save by WordPress's sanitize_title under the site's locale, then every run of underscores or %xx octets turned into one hyphen, repeated hyphens collapsed and hyphens trimmed (SC-014), so it is lower-case letters, digits and single hyphens and never contains __; an empty slug is no anchor; only the slug is stored. At render ids settle in one pass in page order: a landmark clash becomes <anchor>-section, and an id already taken takes the next free -2, -3 (SC-013); ids the system draws are <owner>__<part> and never meet one (markup/section#anchors, SC-012).

maxLines.description: The most lines the text may hold (a street address, two). A limit, held by the limits rule (above): a draft outside it still saves, nothing an editor wrote is cut, and it is checked when the content is published. The emitters record it for each platform's check: ACF also sizes the box to it.

allowed.description: The element kinds an editor may use; both platforms strip anything else. Links allow http, https, mailto and tel. Headings are stored at the level the editor chose, from heading-2 to heading-6, and drawn relative to the heading above the body (markup/section#body-heading-base): the highest-ranked heading in a body draws at base + 1 and the others keep their distance below it.

many.description: An ordered set of images (Payload upload hasMany; ACF gallery).

min.description: The fewest images. A limit, held by the limits rule (above): a draft outside it still saves, nothing an editor wrote is cut, and it is checked when the content is published.

max.description: The most images. A limit, held by the limits rule (above): a draft outside it still saves, nothing an editor wrote is cut, and it is checked when the content is published.

withLabel.description: Whether the link carries its own visible text. Default true.

optionsFrom.description: icons: the options are the contract's content icon names (contract/sections.json, icons.content), plus any a site adds. A default must be one of the contract's.

control.description: radio: the select is drawn as a radio group, on Payload (type radio) and on ACF (type radio) alike. It offers and stores what a select would. Left out, the select is a drop-down. A radio's layout is each platform's to set. A radio cannot be cleared once chosen, so it needs a default or to be required, and its options are the contract's own, never optionsFrom.

min.description: The lowest value. A limit, held by the limits rule (above): a draft outside it still saves, nothing an editor wrote is cut, and it is checked when the content is published.

max.description: The highest value. A limit, held by the limits rule (above): a draft outside it still saves, nothing an editor wrote is cut, and it is checked when the content is published.

min.description: The fewest rows. A limit, held by the limits rule (above): a draft outside it still saves, nothing an editor wrote is cut, and it is checked when the content is published.

max.description: The most rows. A limit, held by the limits rule (above): a draft outside it still saves, nothing an editor wrote is cut, and it is checked when the content is published.

rowLabel.description: The child field whose value names each row in the editor; for a link child, its label.

itemLabel.description: What one row is called, singular.

shape.description: The shape whose fields the group holds (contract/collections/_<shape>.json), in place of fields of its own: address, on a location.

min.description: The fewest items chosen. A limit, held by the limits rule (above): a draft outside it still saves, nothing an editor wrote is cut, and it is checked when the content is published.

max.description: The most items chosen. A limit, held by the limits rule (above): a draft outside it still saves, nothing an editor wrote is cut, and it is checked when the content is published.

sourceField.description: A sibling select whose value is the source id.

modes.description: The modes offered, when not all three.

max.description: The highest count an editor may set. Default 24. The count is a number, and its range a limit held by the limits rule (above).

topicsField.description: The record's own collection's topics, its category terms (one stored name, topics, for every collection; each collection keeps its own list). Only a source with categories (contract/sections.json) has topics. Payload: a relationship to the source's taxonomy collection. ACF: a taxonomy field on the source's taxonomy, which saves nothing to the post's own terms.

dateTimeField.description: A moment, stored as an ISO 8601 date and time in UTC; a view derives the date it draws in the site's time zone. Each platform draws its own picker: Payload date (day and time), ACF date_time_picker.

timeField.description: A time of day, stored as HH:MM on the 24-hour clock (09:00, 17:30). ACF draws its time_picker and returns H:i. Payload has no picker that stores a time alone (its date field stores a whole moment), so the field is text the site draws with a time picker of its own (an admin component), and both platforms refuse any other form on save.

sectionsField.description: A record's body as a list of sections, each stored as on a page (a post's layout). Payload: a blocks field holding those sections' blocks. ACF: a flexible_content field with a layout for each. Used by a collection only.

sections.description: The section ids from contract/sections.json an editor may add, in the order offered.

display.description: On a collection: which stored field fills each part of what the record is drawn as in a section (a card, an FAQ item, an office), for the founder's approval. 'as' names the view-props type (contract/view-props/_shared.json card, faq.json item, locations.json office); each part names a prop of it. A part is filled from one stored field, from several joined, or derived by logic the note describes; a prop the record never fills is left out, and is null.

status.description: draft: proposed, not yet approved by the founder. approved: the founder has approved it.

from.description: The stored field, or fields in order, that fill the part; a path into a group or a list row is dotted (address.street).

join.description: What joins several fields' values, empty ones left out.

allOf.description: The settings file carries no shared settings; every other section file names them.
A collection names its record and has fields of its own, the person shape's, or both.
